title.narrative: Strengthened capacities for development of policies, strategies and implementation of reforms to extend social security coverage

description.narrative: Social protection coverage in Zimbabwe remains limited, leaving a large share of the population exposed to income insecurity and life cycle risks. 2019 estimates indicate that only about 36.7% of the population benefits from at least one social protection or labour programme, while coverage has fluctuated over time and remains uneven. At the labour market level, only around 24% of the working population has access to employment based social security, reflecting the dominance of informality, which accounts for approximately 75% of employment. Pension coverage is also constrained, with roughly 35% of workers contributing to formal pension schemes, and only about 24% of older persons (65+) receiving pensions, underscoring gaps in old age income security. Through the Decent Work Country Programme, the ILO supports strengthening the capacity of national institutions to develop and implement sustainable, effective, inclusive and gender-responsive social protection policies, strategies and legal frameworks; strengthen governance and ensure adequate financing. The strategy focuses on improving system performance, governance and financing, while strengthening the use of integrated policies that link social protection with employment and labour market programmes to support life and work transitions. The ILO is supporting the development of a social protection scheme for the informal economy through building capacities of the National Social Security Authority(NSSA) and knowledge and information sharing with other countries that have implemented similar schemes in South America; and providing technical inputs for the drafting and implementation of the National Social Protection Policy Framework and Strategy through coordinated action with government, social partners and other development partners. Technical assistance is also being extended to deploy the ILO Pension Model (ILO-PENS) for the actuarial valuation of existing NSSA pension schemes.
